persona: Undergraduate finance student completing a managerial-accounting case study: reconciling budget-to-actual monthly cash flow for a small business client (a local cafe) across a fiscal year, pulling budget figures from a planning worksheet and actuals partly from bank-statement PDFs (explains the unicode minus signs) and partly from a general-ledger export (explains the accounting parenthesis negatives and $-formatted text).
source_style: manually maintained Excel cash-flow ledger, with some amounts copy-pasted from a bank statement PDF and a GL export rather than typed fresh, so number formatting is inconsistent across rows

columns.name: Date
columns.notes: Real Excel date (yyyy-mm-dd number format), spaced ~6-7 days apart across Jan-Oct 2025.

columns.name: Category
columns.notes: One of 12 budget-line categories cycled in order: Rent, Payroll, Utilities, Marketing, Software Subscriptions, Travel, Office Supplies, Insurance, Bank Fees, Equipment Lease, Consulting Revenue, Product Sales.

columns.name: Budgeted (USD)
columns.notes: REQUIRED QUIRKS live here: 44 of 50 cells are real Excel numbers (float, '#,##0.00' format). 6 cells are TEXT strings instead: 2 currency-text ('$1,200' row 9, '$3,100' row 28), 2 plain US-thousands-text ('12,345' row 13, '6,750' row 21), 1 unicode-minus text ('−500' row 16), 1 parens-negative text ('(2,000)' row 45).

columns.name: Actual (USD)
columns.notes: REQUIRED QUIRKS live here too: 44 of 50 cells are real Excel numbers. 6 cells are TEXT strings: 2 parens-negative ('(1,200)' row 6, '(450)' row 19), 1 currency-text ('$1,750' row 39), 1 plain US-thousands-text ('9,500' row 31), 2 unicode-minus ('−1,850' row 23, '−12' row 34).

columns.name: Variance (USD)
columns.notes: REQUIRED QUIRK: every one of the 50 rows holds the formula '=E{r}-D{r}' (Actual-Budgeted) written via xlsxwriter with an explicit cached value, so openpyxl(data_only=True) returns a float for all 50 cells (confirmed none are None) even though 12 of those rows reference a text cell that real Excel would show as #VALUE! on a forced recalculation.

columns.name: Account Code
columns.notes: REQUIRED QUIRK: this whole column (G) is hidden via column-level hidden=True; internal GL code 'GL-4001'..'GL-4050', not meant to appear in the printed report.

columns.name: Status
columns.notes: 'Posted' for 47 rows; 'VOID - <reason>' for the 3 rows (Excel rows 11, 26, 47) that are also the REQUIRED hidden rows -- the student hid rather than deleted duplicate/reversed/erroneous entries to keep an audit trail, and those 3 rows should be excluded from any budget-variance analysis.

clean_table.description: 50 data rows, one per transaction, no missing values in any column. To clean: for the 6 messy Budgeted cells and 6 messy Actual cells, strip '$', strip ',' thousands separators, convert a parenthesized amount '(X)' to -X, and convert a unicode minus '−' (U+2212, NOT ASCII hyphen U+002D) prefix to a negative sign, then cast to float. The Variance column's cached formula value already equals Actual_true - Budgeted_true for every row (verified for all 50 by read-back) so it does not need to be recomputed, but a naive Excel recalculation of the 12 rows with text inputs would raise #VALUE!. Exclude the 3 hidden VOID rows before computing any total/average variance.

hidden_void_rows.Status: VOID - duplicate entry (re-keyed same charge twice)
VOID - reversed by bank same day
VOID - data entry error, corrected in the next entry

intended_analysis: Compute total and per-category budget variance (Actual - Budgeted) for the fiscal year, excluding the 3 VOID transactions, to identify which cost/revenue categories are running over or under budget and by how much.
mess_applied: Accounting-style negatives as TEXT in parentheses, e.g. '(1,200)' (3 cells)
US thousands-separator numbers stored as TEXT (no currency/parens), e.g. '12,345' (3 cells)
Unicode MINUS SIGN (U+2212, not ASCII hyphen) as in '−12', pasted from a bank-statement PDF (3 cells)
3 hidden rows (Excel rows 11, 26, 47) holding VOID/duplicate/reversed transactions the student hid instead of deleting
1 hidden column ('Account Code', column G) carrying an internal GL reference not meant for the report
A Variance formula column ('=E{r}-D{r}') with explicit cached values on every row, including the 12 rows whose formula references a text cell
what_a_naive_reader_would_get_wrong: A tool that reads cell values without checking type would silently coerce the 12 messy Budgeted/Actual text cells to NaN/missing (or, worse, mis-parse '(2,000)' as the string 'text' rather than -2000, and '12,345'/'6,750'/'9,500' as unrelated text rather than numbers with commas stripped), undercounting the true totals for those categories. A reader that does not special-case U+2212 (treating it as non-numeric) would fail to parse '−12' and '−1,850' at all, since Python's float() and most numeric coercions only recognize ASCII '-'. A reader using a library that skips hidden rows/columns by default (e.g. some spreadsheet viewers, or pandas with certain engines) would silently drop the 3 VOID rows without the analyst choosing to exclude them -- which happens to be the 'right' outcome here by accident, but for the wrong reason, and would be wrong if a hidden row were NOT supposed to be excluded. Conversely a reader that always includes hidden rows would double-count the duplicate/reversed transactions and inflate variance. A naive reader that also pulls the hidden 'Account Code' column into an analysis (rather than treating it as a hidden internal-only field) would waste effort trying to make a categorical/id column out of what is just a GL reference. Finally, a reader that trusts the Variance column via a full re-open-and-recalculate in Excel (rather than reading the cached value) would see #VALUE! errors on the 12 rows with text inputs, even though the cached value read via openpyxl(data_only=True) is a valid number.
